title: Phase 7: DIPLOMACY - Complete Research with Web Sources
description: Weeks 31-36 - Diplomacy and wars. Research compiled from web sources with detailed implementation.

web_definition.what_is: Diplomacy involves relationships between countries. Key factors: attitude, relations score, infamy, interests.
web_definition.what_exists: Relations: -100 to +100. Attitudes: Hostile, Unfriendly, Neutral, Friendly, Cordial, Allied.
web_definition.how_to_use: Improve relations via diplomatic actions. Attitudes affect AI acceptance of proposals.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Relations change from events, wars, trade. Attitudes calculated from relation score.
web_definition.how_to_expand: Add new diplomatic actions, modify attitude thresholds.

web_definition.what_is: Formal demands that can escalate to war. All wars in Victoria 3 start through diplomatic plays.
web_definition.what_exists: Three phases: Opening Moves (20%), Diplomatic Maneuvering (60%), Countdown to War (20%).
web_definition.how_to_use: Select war goal → add demands → initiate. Countries can join or be swayed. Backing down avoids war.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Maneuvers: ability to sway nations. Infamy: aggression cost. Interests: regional involvement requirement.
web_definition.how_to_expand: Add new war goals, diplomatic play types.

opening_moves.actions: Initial demands, can add primary war goal

diplomatic_maneuvering.actions: Sway nations, add secondary demands, mobilization

countdown_to_war.actions: Lock in, no changes, war begins at 100%

web_definition.what_is: War continues from diplomatic play. Uses fronts, mobilization, and surrender progress.
web_definition.what_exists: Wars have fronts at borders. Units engage in battles. Surrender progress determines victory.
web_definition.how_to_use: Deploy armies to fronts. Mobilize for more battalions. War support affects negotiation.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: War exhaustion from battles. Occupation of states affects surrender progress.
web_definition.how_to_expand: Add unit types, new military mechanics.

war_mechanics.fronts: Created at borders between allied/enemy territory
war_mechanics.occupation: Control states to gain surrender progress

web_definition.what_is: Terms after war ends based on surrender progress and war goals.
web_definition.what_exists: Primary goals (enforced on surrender), secondary goals (negotiated).
web_definition.how_to_use: War leader selects goals from available options. Some goals require meeting surrender threshold.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: War goals define available treaty terms. Infamy affects costs.

web_definition.what_is: Hierarchical relationships between countries. Subject follows overlord's policies.
web_definition.what_exists: Types: Vassal, Puppet, Dominion, Protectorate, Client State.
web_definition.how_to_use: Subjects pay taxes, provide military support. Can have limited diplomacy.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Integrate for full control. Independence movements possible.
web_definition.how_to_expand: Add new subject types with unique mechanics.

web_definition.what_is: Prestige determines international standing. Rank based on prestige with thresholds.
web_definition.what_exists: Six ranks: Great Power, Major Power, Minor Power, Regional Power, Insignificant Power, Unrecognized.
web_definition.how_to_use: Higher rank = more interests, maneuvers, influence capacity. Prestige gained from military, economy, events.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Rank affects diplomatic options. Prestige thresholds: 5× global average for Great Power.

web_definition.what_is: Infamy represents perceived aggression. 0-1000 scale. Higher = more negative diplomatic consequences.
web_definition.what_exists: Four levels: Established (0-25), Disreputable (25-50), Notorious (50-100), Pariah (100+).
web_definition.how_to_use: Aggressive war goals generate infamy. High infamy blocks diplomatic plays by others.
web_definition.how_to_integrate: Infamy calculated: Base × (1 + Pop multiplier) × State multiplier × Rank modifiers.
